7 Relational Data

7.2.1.1 Degree of Nodes

gni reports each node of the current graph: its number, its label, and per value variable the in-degree, out-degree and number of loops. gd4.cf runs it on gd1.dat, which defines two graphs.

Box 182gni (gd4.cf) 

gd1n <- read.table(ex("gd1.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V1", "V2"))
tda_g_nodes(tda_graph(gd1n, directed = TRUE))$table
  V1 V2 V3 V4 V5 V6 V7 V8
1  1  1  1  2  0  2  0  0
2  2  5  1  0  0  0  1  0
3  3  7  1  1  0  1  1  0
4  4  8  0  0  1  0  1  0
5  5  9  0  0  0  0  0  0
6  6 11  0  1  0  1  0  0
7  7 12  1  0  0  0  1  0

Node 8’s first-graph degrees read 0 and 0 here; the manual’s box prints 1 and 1. Running gd4.cf through TDA gives 0 and 0, and so does a build of Rohwer’s unmodified sources, so the box is out of date.

Chapter 7 is relational data. The manual’s example graph is gd1.dat: an edge list I, J with two value variables, V1 and V2, so every node count comes once per value variable. tda_graph() is the gdd command and tda_g_degrees() is gni. A loop (node 8 to itself) is counted in its own column and not in the degrees; the manual’s Box 1 (2002) counted it in both, TDA 6.4p does not.

Box 183gni: in-degree, out-degree and loops per value variable (gd4.cf) 

gd1 <- read.table(ex("gd1.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V1", "V2"))
g1 <- tda_graph(gd1, directed = TRUE)
tda_g_degrees(g1)
  index node in_degree1 out_degree1 loops1 in_degree2 out_degree2 loops2 degree
1     1    1          1           2      0          2           0      0      3
2     2    5          1           0      0          0           1      0      1
3     3    7          1           1      0          1           1      0      2
4     4    8          0           0      1          0           1      0      0
5     5    9          0           0      0          0           0      0      0
6     6   11          0           1      0          1           0      0      1
7     7   12          1           0      0          0           1      0      1

7.2.1.2 Direct Links

tda_g_links() is gdln: for each node the nodes it links to, one ragged record per node with any forward links.

Box 184gdln: forward links 

tda_g_links(g1)$table                     # forward links
  index node n_links links
1     1    1       2  5, 7
2     3    7       1     1
3     4    8       1     8
4     6   11       1    12
tda_g_links(g1, backward = TRUE)$table    # and backward
  V1 V2 V3 V4
1  1  1  1  7
2  2  5  1  1
3  3  7  1  1
4  4  8  1  8
5  7 12  1 11

7.2.2.1 Topological Sorting

tda_g_toposort() is gsort, on the manual’s gd6.dat: a directed acyclic graph, its nodes in an order that respects every edge.

Box 185gsort (gd22.cf) 

gd6 <- read.table(ex("gd6.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
gsrt <- tda_graph(gd6, directed = TRUE)
tda_g_toposort(gsrt)$table
  i node_i label_i
1 1      1       4
2 2      2       5
3 3      4       1
4 4      5       2
5 5      7       3
# option 2 relabels the graph's edges, keeping their values
tda_g_toposort(gsrt, relabel_graph = TRUE)$table
  label_i label_j node_i node_j value
1       1       2      4      5     6
2       1       3      4      7     5
3       1       5      4      2     7
4       2       3      5      7     1
5       2       4      5      1     3
6       3       4      7      1     2
7       3       5      7      2     4
8       4       5      1      2     8

7.2.3.1 Connected Components

tda_g_components() is gcon. gd7.cf declares gd1.dat undirected and valued (gt = 2) and asks for the components of its second graph, the one V2 defines (gn = 2): node 8 joins component 1 through the edge 8-7 that V2 carries and V1 does not.

Box 186gcon: components of graph 2 (gd7.cf) 

gcomp <- tda_graph(gd1, directed = FALSE)
tda_g_components(gcomp, gn = 2)$table
  component n i node_i
1         1 4 1      1
2         1 4 2      5
3         1 4 3      7
4         1 4 4      8
5         2 1 5      9
6         3 2 6     11
7         3 2 7     12
# option 2 lists each component's edges instead, with their values
tda_g_components(gcomp, gn = 2, edges = TRUE)$table
  component n i j node_i node_j value
1         1 4 1 2      1      5     4
2         1 4 1 3      1      7    15
3         1 4 3 4      7      8     0
4         2 1 5 5      9      9    -1
5         3 2 6 7     11     12    14

7.2.3.2 Reachable Nodes in Directed Graphs

gdcon (tda_g(g, "gdcon")) is the directed counterpart of gcon: strongly connected components (opt = 1) or, with opt = 2, the nodes each node reaches. gd8.cf runs it on graph 2 of gd1.dat.

Box 187gdcon: reachable nodes (gd8.cf) (gd30.cf) 

g1d <- tda_graph(gd1, directed = TRUE)
tda_g(g1d, "gdcon", list(gn = 2, opt = 2))$table
4 records, lengths 4-5
[1]  2 5 1 1 
[2]  3 7 1 1 
[3]  4 8 2 1 7 
[4]   7 12  1 11

7.2.6.1 Fundamental Set of Cycles

tda_g_cycles() is gcyc; gd30.cf runs it on gd9.dat, an undirected graph with 6 nodes and 11 edges. opt = 1 lists a fundamental set of cycles, one ragged record each: index, cycle number, length, and the nodes.

gcyc’s four options are four views of the same cycle space. Option 1 lists the nodes of each fundamental cycle, so its rows are ragged; option 2 gives the edge and one indicator per fundamental cycle; option 3 the same over every cycle found; option 4 writes the edges first and then one indicator row per cycle, two row shapes in the one file, which is why it arrives ragged as well.

Box 199gcyc, options 1 to 4 

gd9 <- read.table(ex("gd9.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
g9 <- tda_graph(gd9, directed = FALSE)
tda_g_cycles(g9, "fundamental_nodes")$table

7.3.1.1 The Linear Assignment Problem

tda_gap() is gap: given a cost matrix, the assignment of rows to columns with minimal total cost. The manual’s co1.dat is a 6 x 6 cost matrix, row by row; the result is the permutation of its Box 2 and the matrix with its rows permuted accordingly.

Box 209gap (co1.cf) 

cost <- matrix(scan(ex("co1.dat"), quiet = TRUE), 6, 6, byrow = TRUE)
ap <- tda_gap(cost)
ap$assignment
     [,1] [,2]
[1,]    1    6
[2,]    2    4
[3,]    3    3
[4,]    4    1
[5,]    5    5
[6,]    6    2
ap$permuted
     [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
[1,]    0   76    0   60    0    0
[2,]   24    0   18    0   60   40
[3,]   40    4    2   60    0   16
[4,]   75    3   18    0   55   27
[5,]   53   16   62    0   11   40
[6,]   16   84   10   28    0    4

7.3.1.2 The Quadratic Assignment Problem

tda_gqap() is gqap, on two symmetric matrices, a flow and a distance matrix. co2.dat gives their lower triangles in one file, one pair per line in the order (2,1), (3,1), (3,2); the manual’s Box 2 is the permutation 2, 1, 3.

Box 210gqap (co2.cf) 

co2 <- read.table(ex("co2.dat"), col.names = c("F", "D"))
lower <- function(v) { m <- matrix(0, 3, 3); m[lower.tri(m)] <- v; m + t(m) }
qap <- tda_gqap(lower(co2$F), lower(co2$D))
qap$assignment
[1] 2 1 3
qap$cost
[1] 36
# gqap's second output file: the multigraph under that permutation, with
# the flow and distance between each pair
qap$permuted
  i j node_i node_j flow distance

2 1 2      1      2    1        5
3 1 3      1      3    2        3
4 2 1      2      1    1        5
5 2 2      2      2    0        0
6 2 3      2      3    7        1
7 3 1      3      1    2        3
8 3 2      3      2    7        1
9 3 3      3      3    0        0

7.5.1.1 SAHN Algorithms

tda_cluster() covers TDA’s clustering commands. The manual’s example dissimilarity matrix is cl1.dat, the upper triangle of an 11 x 11 matrix, row by row; cl1.cf runs hcls with opt = 2, complete linkage. The output is the manual’s Box 3: at each level the two clusters merged, named by their representative nodes.

Box 211hcls: complete-link clustering (cl1.cf) (id1.cf) 

D <- scan(ex("cl1.dat"), quiet = TRUE)
dm <- matrix(0, 11, 11)
dm[lower.tri(dm)] <- D
dm <- dm + t(dm)
tda_cluster(dm, method = "hierarchical_single", options = list(opt = 2))$table

2   2  2  1  8
3   3  4  2  9
4   4  7  5 11

6   6 13  3  4
7   7 24  3 10
8   8 33  1  5
9   9 34  3  7
10 10 55  1  3

7.6.1.1 Direct and Indirect Control

tda_gfcf() is gfcf, control in a directed valued graph – gd3.dat is a small ownership network. With sc = 49 (control at more than 49 per cent) node 1 controls nodes 2 to 9, node 9 controls 1 to 8, node 3 controls 5; the pair table of the manual’s Box 2 is the result’s "pairs" attribute.

Box 218gfcf (gd13.cf) 

gd3 <- read.table(ex("gd3.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
ctl <- tda_gfcf(gd3, threshold = 49)
ctl

7.6.1.2 Control

gio computes ownership shares in a directed valued graph: for each pair, the direct share A(i,j) and the share including holdings held through other nodes, Y(i,j). gd11.cf runs it on gd2b.dat.

Box 221gio (gd11.cf) 

gd2b <- read.table(ex("gd2b.dat"), col.names = c("I", "J", "V"))
tda_g_ownership(tda_graph(gd2b, directed = TRUE))$table
   i node_i node_j a_ij      y_ij c iterations
1  1      1      1  0.0 0.0000000 4          4
2  1      1      2  0.5 0.5081285 4          4
3  1      1      3  0.0 0.0812940 4          4
4  1      1      4  0.0 0.1524330 4          4

8  3      3      2  0.1 0.1000000 3          1

10 3      3      4  0.0 0.0300000 3          1

12 4      4      3  0.2 0.2020200 3          2

Two graphs on one page; in the second a reciprocal pair of edges is drawn as two curves, and all edges carry arrowheads.

Box 222gd9.cf 

p <- tda_ps(xlim = c(0, 11.5), ylim = c(0, 4), width = 80, height = 40)

nodesA <- data.frame(id = 1:4, x = c(0.5, 3, 5, 5), y = c(2, 2, 1, 3),
                     grey = 0.8)
edgesA <- data.frame(from = c(1, 2, 2, 4), to = c(2, 4, 3, 3),
                     label = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.2), arrow = "1.5,1.0")
p <- tda_pl_graph(p, nodesA, edgesA)

nodesB <- data.frame(id = 1:4, x = c(6.5, 9, 11, 11), y = c(2, 2, 1, 3),
                     grey = 0.8)
edgesB <- data.frame(from = c(1, 2, 2, 4, 3), to = c(2, 4, 3, 3, 2),
                     label = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.2, 0.1),
                     curve = c(0, 0, 0, 0, -3), arrow = "1.5,1.0")
p <- tda_pl_graph(p, nodesB, edgesB)

p <- tda_pl_text(p, "Graph A", at = c(0.5, 3))
p <- tda_pl_text(p, "Graph B", at = c(6.5, 3))

plot(p)

7.6.1.3 Measures of Flow Centrality

gfc (tda_g(g, "gfc")) is flow centrality on gd14.dat (gd41.cf), one record per pair of nodes.

8 Set-valued Data

Box 224gd40.cf 

p <- tda_ps(xlim = c(0, 8), ylim = c(-1.5, 7), width = 80, height = 40)
nodes <- data.frame(id = 1:5, x = c(1, 3, 5, 3, 7), y = c(3, 6, 3, 0, 3),
                    grey = 0.8)
edges <- data.frame(
    from  = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 3),
    to    = c(2, 3, 4, 3, 3, 5),
    label = c(3, 1, 2, 3, 2, 2),
    arrow = "1.5,1.0")
p <- tda_pl_graph(p, nodes, edges)

plot(p)

8.3.2 Evaluation of Inclusion Functions

Chapter 8 is about set-valued data: a case is not a number but an interval, and the answer is an interval too. tda_evalfi() evaluates a function over interval arguments.

The manual’s box is evalfi1: the function’s inclusion over the interval and its derivative’s, derivative = TRUE.

Box 225An inclusion function and its derivative (evalfi1) 

tda_evalfi("sin(x)", x = c(0, 1))
   lower    upper 
0.000000 0.841471 
tda_evalfi("sin(x)", x = c(0, 1), derivative = TRUE)
    lower     upper 
0.5403023 1.0000000

8.4.1 The gmin Command

tda_gmin() finds the global minimum by subdivision. start= gives the search interval, as c(step, lower, upper); tol_fe= is the tolerance on the function value within which a box is finally accepted. TDA 6.4p’s default is 1e-10, and with it the box containing the minimum of sin(x) on [0, 10] is only temporarily accepted (its lower bound is -1 to sixteen digits, but not to ten); 1e-6 accepts it, giving one box with x in [4.71237, 4.71245].

The manual’s box reports 39 iterations, 41 function evaluations and 77 inclusion evaluations. The program does not: running the manual’s command file unchanged through TDA gives 19, 20 and 35, and so does the call here. The manual is out of date on this box.

Box 226gmin 

g <- tda_gmin("sin(x)", start = list(c(1, 0, 10)), use_derivatives = TRUE,
              tol_fe = 1e-6)
g$value
[1] -1
g$boxes
  box accepted        width lower_f upper_f
1   1        2 7.629395e-05      -1      -1
g$estimates
  box parameter    lower    upper
1   1         x 4.712372 4.712448
# the counters TDA prints above the boxes
g$counts
           iterations           evaluations inclusion_evaluations            boxes_used 
                   19                    20                    35                     3 
      boxes_temporary        boxes_accepted 
                    1                     1

8.6.1 Mean Values

The mean of an interval-valued variable is itself an interval: every value in it is the mean of some admissible data set.
